newsitem.title: CANADA: Pacific Forest workers give strike mandate.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Forest workers give strike mandate.

text.p: Workers at Pacific Forest Products Ltd voted 89 percent in favor of a strike if necessary, the IWA-Canada union said Tuesday.
No date for a strike was set. Canadian unions commonly take a strike vote to strengthen their hand at the bargaining table and only proceed with a strike if talks collapse.

Avenor Inc, which owns 53 percent of Pacific Forest, recently announced a deal to sell its stake to TimberWest Timber Trust. TimberWest in turn plans to sell three Pacific Forest sawmills and forest land to Doman Industries Ltd .
The union said the strike vote was taken because, in its view, Pacific Forest has "attempted to thwart" attempts to negotiate a new labor contract.
The company is not participating in industrywide bargaining under which the union and 65 companies are negotiating a contract in a single set of talks.

The two local unions at Pacific Forest "are hoping that the company will respond to the announcement of the vote and deal with the outstanding issues at its logging and sawmill operations on Vancouver Island," the union said.

Union officials said the pending deal could be positive. "I think the potential sale to TimberWest and Doman will bring some sanity to this situation," said Bill Routley, president of the Duncan local union. "The way Pacific runs things you would think they are looking for a strike."
